d: Optasia is a real-time financial intelligence company. We build precision intelligence that unlocks financial opportunity at scale, running millions of automated credit decisions every day across high-growth markets where formal credit data is limited. Our AI-powered platform turns permitted behavioural data and real-time signals into precise, responsible credit decisions. Embedded within the systems of telcos, banks, digital wallets and other partners, it helps them extend relevant financial services to more people while maintaining strong portfolio control and opens profitable new segments that were previously out of reach. This is how Optasia turns potential into financial progress, responsibly and at scale.

As a New Ventures Business Development Manager for Banks & Payments, you will be responsible for opening and building Optasia's partnerships with financial institutions and the payments ecosystem. You will identify untapped markets and partner segments, such as commercial and digital banks, microfinance institutions, payment service providers, acquirers, mobile money and wallet operators, and remittance players, and turn them into new revenue lines for our AI-driven credit decisioning and financial services platform. You will structure the strategic partnerships behind these ventures, from bank-led lending and funding partnerships to embedded credit at the point of payment, and take each initiative from concept to execution: validating the business case, negotiating the deal, guiding the launch to its first revenue milestones, and handing it over to our regional commercial and operations teams to scale.
q: Proven track record of at least 10+ years' experience in business development, partnerships or corporate development within banking, payments or fintech
Established network across banks, MFIs, payment service providers and mobile money operators, ideally within emerging markets
Demonstrated experience originating and closing bank or payments partnerships and taking them from signature to revenue
Good understanding of retail and SME lending, payment flows, funding structures and the regulatory environment for credit and payments in emerging markets
BSc in Business, Finance, Economics, Engineering or a related field; an MBA or MA/MSc will be considered a plus
Commercial & deal acumen: experience in new business origination, partnership building, contract negotiation, or venture and startup growth within banking and payments ecosystems
Analytical & strategic thinking: ability to evaluate market sizing, competitive dynamics, credit risk and unit economics in ambiguous environments, with strong financial modelling skills
Executive networking: comfort engaging bank and payments decision-makers, regulators, industry leaders and external stakeholders to open doors and build lasting relationships
Excellent communication and presentation skills; fluent in English (French, Arabic or Portuguese will be considered a plus)
Entrepreneurial, self-starter mindset with an owner's sense of accountability
Comfortable working with ambiguity and long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles
Pro-active attitude, hands-on and getting things done
Able to perform under pressure and deliver results in a fast-paced environment, whilst managing several initiatives in parallel
Partner focused, innovative thinking, highly organised with strong attention to detail
Excellent teamwork, influencing and interpersonal skills
Sound judgment, resilience and adaptability to change
Willingness to travel frequently across Optasia's markets
r: Researching new geographies and partner segments across Africa, the Middle East, Asia and Latin America where banks and payment players can extend credit and financial services to underbanked customers through the Optasia platform

Identifying bank and payments use cases, such as credit-as-a-service for banks and digital banks, wallet overdrafts and nano-loans, Buy Now Pay Later at checkout, credit embedded in payment and acquiring flows, and lending linked to remittances
Assessing the needs of partner institutions (customer acquisition, portfolio growth, risk appetite, digital transformation) and of their end customers, and translating them into concrete propositions
Building and maintaining a prioritised pipeline of bank and payments opportunities, supported by market sizing, competitive mapping and an early view of the regulatory and licensing landscape
Tracking banking, payments and fintech trends, regulatory changes, competitor moves and potential partnership or investment targets
Building relationships with CXOs and senior leaders at banks, digital banks, MFIs, payment service providers, acquirers, card schemes and mobile money operators
Structuring commercial agreements, including lending and balance-sheet partnerships, funding facilities, revenue-share models, platform licensing and white-label deals, and joint ventures
Leading negotiations on commercial terms, risk sharing, capital and liquidity requirements, exclusivity and service levels, in close coordination with treasury, finance and legal
Supporting corporate development on the evaluation of strategic investments, acquisitions and bolt-on opportunities in the banking and payments space
Developing pursuit plans and business cases, including P&L projections and unit economics (take rate, credit loss assumptions, cost of funds, interchange and fee structures, operating costs)
Crafting and pitching compelling value propositions to banks and payment partners, occasionally at board and CXO level
Designing pilots and minimum viable launches with clear success criteria, and guiding new partnerships through integration and launch to initial revenue milestones
Monitoring early performance (uptake, repayment, revenue, partner satisfaction) and recommending whether to scale, adjust or stop
Maintaining the CRM pipeline and regular reporting to senior management

Partnering with product, data science and credit risk, technology and integration, finance, treasury, legal, compliance and operations teams to assess the feasibility, risk and regulatory requirements of each opportunity
Coordinating partner due diligence, central bank and licensing assessments, and compliance requirements (KYC, AML, data protection) with internal teams and local advisors
Preparing investment papers and running stage-gate reviews with leadership
Handing off validated partnerships to regional business development and account management teams with a clear launch playbook
x: Optasia is a real-time financial intelligence company turning potential into financial progress.

Our AI-powered platform turns permitted behavioural data and real-time signals into precise, responsible credit decisions. It runs millions of automated decisions every day inside the systems of telcos, banks, digital wallets and other partners, across high-growth markets in Africa, Asia and the Middle East.

The work is demanding, and it matters. You’ll solve for limited formal credit data, unstable connectivity and informal incomes in live production, with risk tightly governed at every step. What you build helps people who were underrepresented in traditional credit histories get practical access to financial services.

We are listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE: OPA), with our head office in Dubai. Our Credo shapes how we work: we start with why, we walk the talk, and we work as One Tribe across teams, countries and cultures.
Flexible working, including our work-from-anywhere policy
Competitive pay and a performance-based bonus scheme
An extra day off on your birthday
The equipment you need to do your best work
Support for your well-being and your career growth

d: The Regulatory Reporting Officer will assist the Finance Manager to ensure compliance of Kuwait branch with regulatory reporting requirements. The incumbent will ensure preparation of periodic Central Bank of Kuwait regulatory reports, returns and requests to the regulatory authorities, in line with0 the guidelines, and support coordination efforts with Central Bank of Kuwait officials/ other regulators /internal stakeholders on matters pertaining to regulatory reporting pertaining to retail/corporate customer segments.
q: University graduate with a degree in Business or Banking or Finance or any other related discipline.
Experience in regulatory reporting in banking industry
r: Verify the balance sheets and related calculations/tables pertaining to the Kuwait branch for review/due submission to the Central Bank of Kuwait, in line with the reporting guidelines.
Ensure timely preparation and submission of all Arabic reports to the regulators.

Assist the Finance Manager in information sourcing / coordination efforts throughout the selection and implementation of applicable Central Bank of Kuwait regulatory reporting tools and interfacing of the same with core banking applications.

Contribute towards and support the Finance Manager in the sharing / implementation of the new CBK Regulatory Reporting requirements that the regulatory agencies/ governmental bodies might enforce, in terms of the policies and operational procedures.
Assist the Finance Manager in periodic monitoring to ensure that adequate internal control procedures are in place to mitigate risk arising out of non-compliance with regulatory framework.

Manage coordination efforts with the internal stakeholders in ensuring prompt submission of statutory and regulatory reporting requirements across the branch in line with the guidelines set by the respective regulatory authorities.
Verify to ensure that reports are completed with a high standard of information integrity and adhere to the reporting deadlines.

Execute coordination efforts with the relevant departments, to ensure preparation / perform due submission of Basel III data (ratios "CAR, LCR, NSFR, LR, DSIB") as per the Central Bank of Kuwait guidelines.
Liaise with the reporting authority to ensure accuracy and clearness of financial data detailed in management reports / data produced for Central Bank of Kuwait.

Support the Finance Manager in coordination efforts with the IT Department for the development of new / continuous improvement in report requirements, as directed by the Central Bank of Kuwait over the time.
Reconcile and ensure submission of the cash/Credit Classification for the branch within the prescribed timeframe and as per guidelines.
